transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
The backlash against President Trump's immigration enforcement tactics played a role in this
week's Republican losses, especially in Texas.
Now, as NPR's Sergio Martinez-Beltron reports, Democrats are weighing a seismic political
shift that many see as a mandate on immigration policy.
Exit polling shows immigration was top of mind for voters.
In Texas, two men have been killed by ICE agents, including Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in
Houston who was shot to death on his way to work.
His son, Ronaldo Salgado, says the results should make the new Democratic majority reflect.
Unfortunately, Texas has become like the epicenter of ICE enforcement and like gross violence
against immigrants and the voters spoken, the incoming lawmakers have a duty to listen
to us.
Locally, immigrant rights advocates say they want the state to stop collaborating with
ICE.
Nationally, they want less funding for ICE and oversight.
Sergio Martinez-Beltron, NPR News, Austin, Texas.
Democratic Senator Chris Murphy is out of the hospital less than a week after having
a stroke.
As Molly Ingram of Member Station WSHU reports, he's now headed to rehab.
In his first statement since suffering a stroke last Saturday, Murphy says he was diagnosed
with a small bleed in the thalamus region of his brain.
The 53-year-old said he felt numbness in his arm while at his son's hockey game and decided
to call 911.
Murphy said the experience has been scary for him and his family and thanked doctors
and staff at the Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore.
According to his office, Murphy will spend the next several weeks in rehab and will miss
votes while he recovers.
His doctor said in a statement that Murphy was making tremendous progress and is expected
to make a full recovery.
For NPR News, I'm Molly Ingram in Fairfield, Connecticut.
The nation's Oregon transplantation system today adopted emergency rules designed to improve
the safety of a controversial new form of organ procurement.
Here's Rob Stein has more.
The Oregon Procurement and Transplantation Network's board of directors approved new
rules for a type of organ donation known as NRP.
The procedure involves restarting circulation quickly after a potential donor has been declared
dead because their heart stopped.
NRP was developed to obtain more organs for transplants, but critics say the procedure
violates the fundamental rules for how donors are declared dead.
The new policy was developed after concerning reports of blood flow possibly returning to
the brains of NRP donors after they were declared dead.
The new policy could be revised after the public has a chance to weigh in.
Rob Stein, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
In Europe, officials say more bomb threats were made against flights following a series
of hoaxes that have caused flight diversions this week.
Three broadcasters have also received security threats, and while no suspicious items have
been found, the threats have raised concern amid other recent disruptions.
France's prime minister says four bomb threats targeted aircraft over French territory, and
Hungary's defense minister, says military fighter jets, escorted three passenger planes
through the country's airspace.
There are several other threats to flights, and it's not clear who's behind it all.
Zoo Atlanta's newest pandas have made their public debut.
As Marisa Meckie of member station WABE reports, Atlanta is now one of three zoos in the country
housing giant pandas.
Jessica Hogan lives just down the street from Zoo Atlanta, and she and her three kids come
several times a week.
My one-year-old has been asking for the pandas for about a week now.
Male panda Ping Ping and female Fu Shuang made their first public appearance after arriving
from China in late September.
Chinese ambassador to the U.S. Ciafeng says the pandas are a symbol of peace between the
two nations.
"Now there's one Chinese ambassador in D.C., but Atlanta alone boasts two panda envoys
who are both much weightier than me."
For now, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are getting to know each other and their new neighbors
here in Atlanta.
For NPR News, I'm Marisa Meckie in Atlanta.
And I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.
Making up first takes overnight shifts from dedicated journalists across the country, and
it's only possible with listener support.

Give a little and get more NPR, all in less time.

topics.text: Immigration enforcement backlash, especially ICE killings in Texas, factors into this week's Republican losses
Sen. Chris Murphy leaves Johns Hopkins hospital after a stroke, heads to rehab, expected to fully recover
Oregon transplant network adopts emergency rules for NRP organ procurement, a controversial donor procedure
Bomb threats against European flights, including in France and Hungary, prompt diversions and escorts by fighter jets
Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang make public debut at Zoo Atlanta after arriving from China
